evals.name: simple-technical-spike-create
evals.prompt: Read the linkbox README. We need a spike for LB-441 -- can you write one up for the Postgres full-text search vs. dedicated search index question?
evals.expected_output: Classifies this as an Exploration-type technical spike comparing two concrete options and writes a document with the skill's full mandatory structure, including a falsifiable, directional Hypothesis (not a restatement of the question) and time-bound Acceptance Criteria tied to evaluation/learning rather than to shipping or picking a winner.

assertions.text: Document uses the skill's full mandatory structure, including a dedicated 'Hypothesis' section and a dedicated 'Acceptance Criteria' section (not folded into a general recommendation or background writeup)
Hypothesis is stated as a falsifiable, directional belief ('we believe X will produce outcome Y') rather than a restatement of the question or an open-ended investigation prompt
Acceptance criteria are bound to time-spent/learning-produced ('we have spent N days evaluating...', 'we have documented...') rather than to shipping or choosing a specific implementation
Spike is classified with an explicit type label (e.g. 'Exploration') appropriate to a two-option technical comparison, per the skill's type-detection guidance

evals.name: safe-enabler-story-spike
evals.prompt: Read the ledgerflow README. We need a spike written up for the LEDG-EPIC-12 event-streaming viability question ahead of PI Planning.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this as a SAFe Enabler-workflow spike ahead of PI Planning and produces a document with a structured Stakeholders and Demo Audience table, checkbox-style acceptance criteria reflecting the Enabler workflow, a 'Shared to' checklist in Findings for System Demo/ART/Enabler Story tracking, and a Risks section that explicitly names the risk of missing the System Demo/PI Planning date.

assertions.text: Document includes a structured 'Stakeholders and Demo Audience' table naming the ART/team, System Demo date, requesting stakeholder, and other interested parties -- not just loose mentions of these in prose or a header
Findings section includes a 'Shared to' checklist tracking whether the spike was demonstrated at the System Demo, shared with the ART, and reflected in the Enabler Story ticket
Acceptance criteria are written as checkbox items reflecting a SAFe Enabler workflow (e.g. timebox elapsed, approaches evaluated, findings documented, presented at System Demo, Enabler Story updated)
Risks and Open Questions explicitly names the risk that missing the System Demo / PI Planning date delays Epic sizing to the next PI, not just a generic 'timebox may be tight' risk

evals.name: update-mode-anti-pattern-audit
evals.prompt: Read the catalog-service README, then read and clean up the spike document it references at docs/spikes/2026-08-01-technical-spike-redis-cache.md.
evals.expected_output: Audits and updates the existing spike document in place: rewrites the Hypothesis into falsifiable, directional form, turns the Evidence and Links section into actual links (or explicit TODO placeholders) instead of unlinked prose, makes the Timebox's hard stop explicit and independent of completion status, and preserves the original document's substantive load-testing methodology and results while fixing these structural anti-patterns.

assertions.text: Hypothesis is rewritten into falsifiable, directional form ('we believe X will produce outcome Y, which will allow us to Z') rather than left as or reworded into an open-ended 'we will investigate whether...' statement
'Evidence and Links' section is rewritten as an actual list of links (or explicit TODO link placeholders), not left as prose describing a spreadsheet or screenshots without linking to them
Timebox section states the hard stop explicitly as independent of completion status (e.g. 'regardless of completion status'), not just that the timebox 'was fully used' or 'closed on schedule'

Findings section retains and preserves the substantive load-testing methodology and results from the original document (concurrency levels tested, cache hit rate methodology, memory/eviction checks) rather than being thinned out while fixing the structural anti-patterns
